result.evidence: The hypothesis applies the biological mechanism of Physarum polycephalum network adaptation to traffic signal systems. While the source document describes how slime mold creates efficient networks through local feedback rules (thickening tubes with high flow, thinning those with low flow), the hypothesis transfers this concept to traffic systems with different parameters (queue length, throughput, phase timing). The mapping requires abstracting the biological mechanism to a general principle of local rules creating system-wide optimization, then applying it to a completely different domain (traffic engineering). This is not a direct restatement or composition of the source content, but a genuine cross-domain transfer inspired by the biological example.
